regras/competencias/atirador.title: Marksman
regras/competencias/atirador.summary: Marksman represents the character who prepares their shots and keeps their Aim to hit a target with precision. Its Capabilities apply to any Attack with the Shooting Skill.
regras/competencias/atirador.text:
Marksman represents the character who prepares their shots and keeps their Aim to hit a target with precision. Its Capabilities apply to any Attack with the Shooting Skill.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Shooting Stance 
2 Unshakable Focus 
3 Steady Aim 
4 Improved Shooting Stance 
5 Unwavering Focus 
Level 1 — Shooting Stance
During your Turn, before making an Attack with the Shooting Skill, if you have not moved yet, you can take a Shooting Stance until the end of the Turn. While in this stance:
you get +2 dice to the Pool of Attacks made with Shooting;
you ignore the first -2 dice penalty for attacking beyond the weapon's normal range;
you cannot move until the end of the Turn.
Level 2 — Unshakable Focus
At the start of your Turn, if you have no Aiming stacks, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action.
In addition, being forcibly moved does not make you lose your Aiming stacks. You still lose them if you take damage or another usual condition for losing the Aim happens.
Level 3 — Steady Aim
While in the Shooting Stance, you can move up to half your base Movement during the Turn, instead of staying still.
This move does not make you lose your Aiming stacks.
Level 4 — Improved Shooting Stance
While in the Shooting Stance, you can take any amount of superficial Willpower damage. For each point taken, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action. The stack limit set by your Cunning still applies, and points taken beyond that limit grant no stacks. With a full Willpower track, each point can be paid by Breaking Limit.
Level 5 — Unwavering Focus
Your Unshakable Focus evolves. At the start of your Turn, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action, even if you already have stacks.
In addition, the maximum number of Aiming stacks you can have becomes:
Cunning + Marksman Level
This limit replaces the one set by Cunning in every rule, including Improved Shooting Stance.

regras/competencias/cacador.text:
Hunter represents the character who lives off the wilds and the creatures that dwell in them. They follow tracks others cannot see, know the animals, monsters and supernatural creatures they pursue in depth and use that knowledge to bring them down.
This Competency's Capabilities use the Survival Skill, the Nature Specific Knowledge: in-depth knowledge of the fauna, flora, terrain and climate of the wilds; and the Occultism Skill. Without a Level in Nature or Occultism, the Pool uses Cunning alone.
A prey is a creature of any Type except Humanoid. Against Beast, Plant, Monstrosity and Dragon, the study uses Nature; against Undead, Construct, Elemental, Spirit and Aberration, it uses Occultism.
Progression
Level Capability granted Weak Spot 
1 Tracker — 
2 Know the Prey — 
3 Hunter's Strike — 
4 Weak Spot +4 
5 Relentless Hunt +5 
Level 1 — Tracker
You get +2 dice on Survival tests to follow tracks and to erase your group's tracks.
When you successfully follow tracks, you also learn which creature left them, how many there are, how long ago they passed and whether they were wounded or in a hurry.
Level 2 — Know the Prey
You can use your Action to study a prey you can observe. Test Cunning + Nature or Cunning + Occultism, depending on the prey's Type, against a Difficulty set by the Narrator.
Whatever the result, the prey becomes Read by you until the end of the Scene. You cannot study a prey already Read by you.
Success: you ask the Narrator 1 question from the list below, plus 1 for each Success above the Difficulty.
Failure: you find out nothing.
Questions:
What is one of its Resistances or Immunities?
What is one of its Vulnerabilities?
What is one of its Traits?
How does it hunt, attack or defend itself?
Is it wounded, hungry or cornered?
Each question reveals a single Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability or Trait. When the prey has none, the Narrator says so.
When following a prey's tracks with Tracker, you can make this test from the tracks, without spending an Action. The prey becomes Read by you during the first Scene in which you find it.
Level 3 — Hunter's Strike
You get +2 dice when starting a Confrontation with an Attack against a prey Read by you.
Level 4 — Weak Spot
When you attack a prey Read by you with a Damage Type or Material to which it has a Vulnerability, the weapon's Damage increases by an amount equal to your Hunter Level: +4 at Level 4 and +5 at Level 5.
The bonus applies to any kind of Attack, including on a tie, when the weapon's Damage is dealt as superficial damage. It does not add dice to the Pool.
Level 5 — Relentless Hunt
When you study a prey, you can mark it as your hunt. It remains Read by you across Scenes until it dies or you mark another. You can only have one hunt at a time.
You always know in which direction your hunt is, as long as it is in the wilds and within a day's travel of you.

regras/competencias/furioso.text:
Furious represents the fighter who trades defense for aggression and turns pain and Willpower into brute force.
Fury is not a core Condition: its rules are set only in this Competency.

1 Fury 
2 Blood for Blood 
3 Furious Charge 
4 Beyond Pain

Level 1 — Fury
During combat, on your Turn, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to enter Fury. Entering Fury does not spend your Action.
Fury lasts until the end of your next Turn. Whenever you start a Confront with a melee Attack or a thrown weapon, the duration is extended until the end of your following Turn. Accepting the Confront does not extend Fury. It also ends at the end of combat.
While in Fury:
you can use Strength instead of the Attribute normally set for melee Attacks;
you get +2 dice to the Pool when starting a melee Confront;
you suffer −2 dice to the Pool when Defending and Dodging. Accepting the Confront does not suffer this penalty.
Level 2 — Blood for Blood
While in Fury, your melee Attacks get a bonus to weapon damage according to the damage marked on your Health track:
+1 for each point of superficial damage;
+2 for each point of aggravated damage.
The bonus is calculated when the Attack's damage is applied and is added to the weapon's damage bonus in every situation in which it is dealt, including on a tie, when the damage is dealt as superficial damage.
This bonus adds no dice to the Pool and does not apply to the counterattack when Accepting the Confront.
Level 3 — Furious Charge
While in Fury, your base Movement increases by +2 squares.
In addition, on entering Fury, you immediately get the effect of the Run Action on that Turn, without spending your Action. The Movement increase also applies to this Run.
Level 4 — Beyond Pain
While in Fury:
you ignore the Debilitated penalty;
you do not receive Fear stacks. On entering Fury, you lose every Fear stack you have.
When Fury ends, effects that would apply Fear again work as usual from that moment on. Stacks lost on entering Fury do not come back.
Level 5 — Refuse to Fall
While in Fury, having your whole Health track filled with aggravated damage does not leave you incapacitated right away. You keep acting as usual, but at the start of each of your Turns in this situation you must take 1 point of aggravated Willpower damage to stay on your feet.
In addition, each instance of Health damage you take in this situation, from any source, causes 1 point of aggravated Willpower damage, whatever the amount of damage dealt.
You become incapacitated when:
you decide not to take the Willpower damage at the start of your Turn;
your whole Willpower track is filled with aggravated damage;
Fury ends, including at the end of combat.

regras/competencias/guardiao.title: Guardian
regras/competencias/guardiao.summary: Guardian represents the shield fighter who plants themselves between danger and those at their side, protecting themselves and extending their defense to their allies. The Capabilities of this Competency require you to…
regras/competencias/guardiao.text:
Guardian represents the shield fighter who plants themselves between danger and those at their side, protecting themselves and extending their defense to their allies.
The Capabilities of this Competency require you to be holding a Shield and use only its Protection. They do not apply without a Shield in hand, nor to Parry.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Cover Ally 
2 Shield Mastery 
3 Intercept 
4 Shelter 
5 Bulwark 
Level 1 — Cover Ally
Once per Round, when an ally adjacent to you is the target of an Attack, they add your Shield's Protection to their own Pool if they choose to Defend or Dodge. They can Defend even without a Shield:
Defend = the ally's Strength + Fighting + your Shield's Protection
Dodge = the ally's Agility + Acrobatics + your Shield's Protection
If the ally Defends holding a Shield of their own, they use the higher Protection of the two. The Protections do not stack.
You decide to use Cover Ally after the Attack is declared and before the ally chooses their response. If they Accept the Confront, the use for the Round is lost.
You cannot Cover an ally while you are surprised, incapacitated or Paralyzed.
Level 2 — Shield Mastery
Shields you hold have their Minimum Strength reduced by 1 and do not impose the Heavy Shield's -1 die when Attacking penalty.
Level 3 — Intercept
When an ally adjacent to you is the target of an Attack, before they choose their response, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to swap places with them and become the target of the Attack.
You must respond to the Confront by Defending. The Attack keeps the Pool the attacker has already built.
Swapping places does not spend Movement and does not trigger effects caused by movement. If either of you does not fit in the other's space, you cannot Intercept.
In addition, Cover Ally improves: after the first use in a Round, you can use it again by taking 1 point of superficial Willpower damage for each additional use.
Level 4 — Shelter
When resisting a damage Zone, you can add your Shield's Protection to your own test Pool or to the Pool of an adjacent ally resisting the same Zone. The Protection applies to only one of these Pools.
If the chosen ally is holding a Shield, they use the higher Protection of the two. The Protections do not stack.
Level 5 — Bulwark
When Defending using your Shield's Protection, you win on a tie: the Attack is blocked and no one takes damage.
This also applies to the ally who Defends through Cover Ally.

What do they want at this moment?
Are they hiding something? (yes or no)
What or whom are they afraid of?
What is one true fact about their life, such as their trade, their origin or a close relationship?
Questions about strengths and weaknesses:

What is one of their Vulnerabilities?

You get a number of extra dice equal to your Mentalist Level on every Cunning + Perception test, including Cold Read.

regras/competencias/sentinela.text:
Sentinel represents the fighter who controls the space around them, punishing anyone who tries to escape their weapon's reach and anyone who attacks their allies.

Level 1 — Opportunity Attack

The Attack happens before it leaves the Reach. Once it is resolved, the creature continues its Turn normally, if it can.
The target can only respond by Defending, which includes Parry, or Dodging. It cannot Accept the Confront.
Forced movement, such as from a Maneuver, and the movement of a won Dodge do not provoke an Opportunity Attack.
Level 2 — Halt
When you win an Opportunity Attack other than on a tie, the target's remaining Movement for that Turn becomes 0. It cannot move any more that Turn, not even by Running, but it can still use its Action in other ways.
On a tie, the Attack deals the normal tie damage and the target continues moving.
Level 3 — Retaliate
An Opportunity Attack can also be provoked when an enemy creature within your melee weapon's Reach starts a Confront against one of your allies. You attack after that Confront is resolved.
This use follows the same rules and the same per-Round limit, and Halt also applies to it.
Level 4 — Tireless Vigilance
After the first Opportunity Attack in a Round, you can make more by taking 1 point of superficial Willpower damage for each additional use.
Each movement or Confront provokes at most one Opportunity Attack from you.

regras/criaturas/caracteristicas-de-npc.text:
NPC Traits are abilities belonging to NPCs, creatures and enemies. They are set directly on the creature's sheet and are not part of the characters' Competency system.
Configurable values
Each trait comes with default values in parentheses, such as Potency, the Pool used to resist, the duration or the number of stacks. These values are configurable on each creature: two creatures with the same trait can have different values.
Potency is the Difficulty of the test the target makes to resist, when the trait calls for one.
When a Trait mentions a Skill without spelling out the full Pool, it uses the Skill's linked Attribute. Pools expressly made of two Attributes, such as Vigor + Determination, stay unchanged.
Special movement
Swimming and climbing are Special Movement and cost 2 Movement points per square. With one of these traits, the creature uses that movement at the normal cost, 1 point per square, and chooses on its Turn whether to spend its Movement on normal or special movement.
Aquatic and Flying can come with a value in parentheses, such as Aquatic (5): it is the creature's Movement in that medium, also at the normal cost. With no value, it uses its default Movement. A creature that only moves in water, such as a shark, has Movement 0 on land.
Aquatic
Description: swims at the normal cost and breathes underwater. With a value, swims with that Movement.
Flying
Description: flies at the normal cost (see Flight), with the value's Movement when there is one, and ignores Difficult Terrain on the ground. If it becomes Prone or Grappled in the air, it falls.
Burrowing
Description: digs and moves through the earth at the normal cost. While buried, it cannot be the target of Attacks.
Climbing
Description: climbs walls and ceilings at the normal cost, without needing a test.
On-hit effects
When the creature wins an Attack with a melee natural Attack, the target makes a test to resist, with Difficulty equal to the Potency. On a failure, they suffer the effect.
Venomous (Potency 2; Vigor + Determination)
Description: a target who fails becomes Poisoned for a number of Turns equal to the Potency.
Paralyzing (Potency 2; Vigor + Strength)
Description: a target who fails becomes Paralyzed for 1 Turn.
Stunning (Potency 2; Determination + Cunning)
Description: a target who fails becomes Stunned for 1 Turn.
Infectious
Description: the disease or curse transmitted, the Pool to resist, the Potency and the duration are set on each creature (for example, lycanthropy).
Special attacks
Frenzy
Description: once per Turn, on winning an Attack, the creature makes another Attack against another adjacent target, with -2 dice.
Improved Frenzy
Requirement: Frenzy
Description: Frenzy's extra Attack does not suffer the penalty.
Breath (Damage; Damage Type)
Description: with its Action, the creature creates an instant Zone in a 3-square cone. The Zone has the Damage and Damage Type set on the creature. Breath cannot be used on consecutive Turns.
Charge (+2 Damage; 4 squares)
Description: if the creature moves at least 4 squares in a straight line before attacking, it adds +2 to the Damage of the Attack.
Go for the Throat (Margin 3)
Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 3 or more, the damage ignores the Absorption of the target's armor. Base Absorption still applies.
Constrictor (Margin 2)
Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 2 or more, the target also becomes Grappled. At the start of each of the creature's Turns, whoever it is grappling takes the Damage of its natural Attack.
Terrifying (Potency 2; Determination + Cunning; stacks equal to Potency)
Description: whoever sees the creature for the first time in the scene makes the test to resist. Whoever fails receives stacks of Fear. It happens once per scene for each character.
Web (Potency 2; Attack: Agility + Shooting; escape: Strength + Athletics)
Description: the creature makes a ranged Attack with Agility + Shooting. A sheet can expressly set another Attack Attribute for its Web. On a win, it leaves the target Grappled by the web. To break free, the target uses their Action and tests Strength + Athletics against the Potency.
Burrowing Ambush
Requirement: Burrowing
Description: when coming out of the ground to attack, the creature tests Agility + Stealth against the target's Cunning + Perception. If it wins, it gets +2 dice on the Attack.
Swarm (damage by Size)
Description: the creature is a swarm of small critters, treated as a single one. At the start of each of its Turns, every creature inside the token or adjacent to it takes superficial damage, with no Attack roll. The base damage comes from Size (Medium 2, Large 4, Huge 6) and drops by 1 for each creature hit beyond the first, to a minimum of 1. The creature's on-hit effects, such as Venomous, apply to each creature hit. The base damage can change on each creature. It is usually Immune to Slashing and Piercing.
Recovery
Regeneration (2; interrupted by the Damage Type or Material set on the creature)
Description: at the end of each of its Turns, the creature converts a number of points of aggravated damage to superficial equal to its Regeneration value, without needing treatment. The value is configurable on each creature.
Interruption: each creature lists the Damage Types or Materials that interrupt its Regeneration. If it took damage from one of them since the end of its last Turn, it does not regenerate on that Turn. The interruption lasts only that Turn: on the next Turn, with no new damage of that type, Regeneration comes back.
Senses
Darkvision (12 squares)
Description: up to its range, the creature ignores the Dim and Dark penalties, but sees without telling colors apart. Beyond its range, Lighting applies as usual. Pitch black, magical darkness, blocks Darkvision.

regras/movimento/movimentacao.title: Movement

regras/movimento/movimentacao.text:
During their Turn, a character can move across the battlefield using their Movement.
By default, every character has a base Movement of 6 squares per Turn.
Base Movement: 6 squares
Effects that reduce or increase a character's Movement change their base Movement. While the effect lasts, every rule that uses base Movement uses the modified value.
Movement can happen before or after the character's Action, in whatever order they prefer.
Moving Around
Each square moved costs 1 point of Movement.
Moving diagonally also costs only 1 point of Movement. Astra does not use extra costs for diagonal movement.
A character can move through a square occupied by an ally normally (but cannot stay in the same square), but cannot move through a square occupied by an enemy.
Difficult Terrain
Certain spaces can count as Difficult Terrain, representing surfaces or obstacles that slow movement down.
Each square of Difficult Terrain costs 2 points of Movement to cross.
For example, a character with 6 points of Movement could normally cross 6 squares, but only 3 squares if the whole path were Difficult Terrain.
Movement and Enemies
Moving out of an enemy's reach does not, by default, provoke Attacks or other penalties.
Certain Capabilities, Traits or effects can create exceptions to this rule, letting a character punish or interfere with their opponents' movement.
Special Movement
Special Movement is any form of movement different from the character's ordinary movement on land.
This includes situations such as swimming, climbing, crawling, squeezing through tight spaces or any other form of locomotion that requires effort, technique or conditions different from normal movement.
Each square covered using Special Movement costs 2 points of Movement.
1 square of Special Movement = 2 points of Movement
Costs add up. A square of Difficult Terrain crossed with Special Movement costs 4 points of Movement.
Normally, swimming and climbing do not require a roll. When the risk, pressure or difficulty of the situation calls for a test, the standard Pool is Strength + Athletics. Long trials of endurance or exhaustion may call for a separate Vigor test, depending on the situation.
Flight
Flight does not use the Special Movement rules.
How a character flies, their speed, limitations, costs and other properties are set directly by the Capability, Trait, equipment, effect or other source that grants that ability.
This way, different forms of flight can work in different ways, depending on their origin.
Jumping
A Jump is made using an Action and has its own rules. See Jump.

regras/movimento/correr.text:
When using the Run Action, the character increases how far they can move during the Turn.
The character gets additional squares of Movement equal to their base Movement for that Turn.
Since base Movement is 6 squares by default, this usually grants +6 squares, letting them cover up to:
12 squares
Run is an automatic Action and requires no test.
The character does not need to use their Movement before choosing Run. When taking this Action, the additional squares are simply added to the Movement available that Turn.
Characters with a base Movement other than 6 get a bonus equal to their own base Movement. A character with a base Movement of 8 squares, for example, gets +8 squares when Running, and can cover up to 16 squares.

regras/movimento/saltar.title: Jump
regras/movimento/saltar.summary: When using the Jump Action, the character makes a horizontal or vertical jump. The base distance of the Jump is equal to half of the character's Strength, rounded down. Base Jump distance = Strength ÷ 2 (rounded down).
regras/movimento/saltar.text:
When using the Jump Action, the character makes a horizontal or vertical jump.
The base distance of the Jump is equal to half of the character's Strength, rounded down.
Base Jump distance = Strength ÷ 2 (rounded down)
Run-up
Before Jumping, the character can use part of their Movement to get a Run-up.
Each square covered before the jump adds +1 square to the total distance reached.
The maximum Run-up that can be used is equal to the character's Athletics, with a minimum of 1 square.
Maximum Run-up = Athletics
Characters with Athletics 0 can still use up to 1 square of Run-up.
The character does not have to use all of the available Run-up. Only the squares actually covered before the Jump are added to the distance.
The total distance is the base distance plus the Run-up used.
Jump distance = half of Strength + Run-up
A Jump does not require a roll. As long as the intended distance is within the character's limit, they can make it using their Action.
Vertical Jump
The same rules can be used to determine the height reached by a Jump.
In that case, the maximum height the character can reach is equal to half of the calculated distance, rounded down.
Jump height = Jump distance ÷ 2 (rounded down)
When you need to express that height or distance in physical units, use:
1 square = 5 feet = 1.5 meters
This conversion is only a narrative reference and does not change how the rule works in squares.
Example
A character has:
Strength 4
Athletics 3
Their base Jump distance is 2 squares.
Since they have Athletics 3, they can use up to 3 squares of Run-up. If they cover the 3 squares before taking the Jump Action, they can reach:
2 + 3 = 5 squares
If they cover only 1 square before the jump, they reach 3 squares.
On a Vertical Jump with the same 3 squares of Run-up, they would reach 2 squares of height.

regras/equipamentos/equipamentos.text:
Equipment is the objects characters carry and use, whether to attack, protect themselves or carry out other tasks.
The Astra core currently organizes equipment into four types:
Weapons — equipment used to attack.
Armor — equipment used for protection.
Shields — equipment used for defense.
Common items — everyday objects, such as backpacks, ropes and tools.
The equipment available in the core is gathered in:
Weapon Catalog;
Armor Catalog;
Shield Catalog.
New equipment types may be added in the future, through specific modules or settings.
Value
All equipment has a Value, used to compare prices and build budgets. Value is an abstract number and may have decimals; the setting decides the currency's name, its availability and the buying rules.
Use during scenes
Switching Equipment — the action used to replace an item that is already in use.
Scenes and Conflicts — rules for confrontations and other tactical decisions.
Load
The weight of equipment is not measured in kilograms. In Astra, the space an item takes up is measured in slots.
Each piece of equipment has a Load value, which tells how many slots it takes. This applies equally to weapons, armor, shields and common items.
Maximum Load
A character's Maximum Load is the total Load they can carry without penalties. Its standard formula is:
5 + Strength slots
Strength is the Load Attribute by default. Capabilities and other rules can replace it in this formula. When that happens, Maximum Load is recalculated immediately from the new Attribute, without changing Strength tests or other rules.
Overload
Carrying more than the Maximum Load leaves the character in Overload. While in Overload, they:
have their base Movement cut in half (see Movement);
suffer -2 dice on rolls that use a Physical Attribute.
Overload ends as soon as the Load is back within the limit.

Field Description

A weapon's Properties are organized into five categories. Every weapon has exactly one Origin and one Material; the Grip, Use and Special properties are optional and can be combined as the weapon's entry says.

Crafted — a weapon made to be used as a weapon. This is the default origin.

Material represents a category that matters for defenses, rather than telling apart every common raw material.
Material Covers 
Organic Body, flesh, claws, fangs, bones and shells 
Wood Common wood and other plant materials used in weapons 
Stone Rock, flint, obsidian and common minerals 
Common metal Iron, steel, bronze, copper and other common alloys

Meteorite Special material, with its own interaction with defenses

Two-handed — a weapon that must be held in both hands to be used.
Flexible — a weapon that can be used in one hand or both. Held in both hands, it gets +1 Damage.

The second target must be within the weapon's reach and adjacent to the original target; they do not make another roll to respond.

Debilitating (Slowed) — on winning an Attack, the attacker can give up the weapon's Damage. The target takes only the Margin and becomes Slowed.

Physical: Slashing, Bludgeoning, Piercing
Elemental: Fire, Ice, Electric, Acid, Poison
Magic: Magic
Each damage source defines its Damage Type — for example, a sword deals Slashing, a mace deals Bludgeoning and a fire spell deals Fire. Catalogs and modules can add new damage types.

regras/equipamentos/armaduras.text:
Armor is equipment used to protect the character.
The armor available in the core is in the Armor Catalog.
Each armor is described by the following fields:
Field Description 
Name the armor's name 
Category Light, Medium or Heavy (see Categories) 
Minimum Strength the Strength needed to wear the armor without losing Movement 
Description a short description of the armor 
Absorption how many points of aggravated damage are converted into superficial 
Properties the armor's special traits 
Load how many slots the armor takes 
Value the armor's cost 
Absorption
An armor's Absorption tells how much aggravated damage taken is converted into superficial damage.
When taking damage from an Attack, the character converts to superficial a number of points of aggravated damage equal to their Absorption — never more than the aggravated damage taken. Total Absorption is the sum of the character's base Absorption and the Absorption of the equipped armor. Base Absorption can be raised or lowered by effects, but never goes below 0.
For example: an armor with Absorption 2 takes an Attack that deals 3 aggravated damage. 2 points are converted into superficial damage, and only 1 point stays aggravated.
Damage that is already superficial is not affected: armor only reduces how much damage stays aggravated.
Resistances and Vulnerabilities to specific Damage Types can raise or lower this absorption (see Resistance and Vulnerability).
Categories
Every armor has a Category, which organizes its Absorption, Dodge penalty, Minimum Strength and typical Load.
Category Absorption When Dodging Minimum Strength Load 
Light 1 no penalty — 1 
Medium 2 to 3 -2 to -3 dice 2 2 
Heavy 4 to 5 -4 to -5 dice 3 3 to 4 
Dodge: with Medium or Heavy armor, the Dodge Pool loses dice equal to the armor's Absorption. The character's base Absorption and Resistances do not count.
Minimum Strength: with Strength below the Minimum Strength of the armor worn, the character has -2 Movement.
Properties
Properties are an armor's special traits. The starting list of properties is:
[Type] Resistance (value) — the armor grants Resistance to the given Damage Type. The value is added to Effective Absorption against that Type — for example, an armor with Absorption 2 and Slashing Resistance 1 has Effective Absorption 3 against Slashing and 2 against the other Types.
[Type] Vulnerability (value) — the armor leaves the wearer vulnerable to the given Damage Type. The value is subtracted from Effective Absorption against that Type — for example, metal armors have Electric Vulnerability 1: a Chain Mail with Absorption 4 ends up with 3 against Electric.
Modules and settings can add new properties and armors to the core catalog.

regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.title: Switching Equipment
regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.summary: Drawing a piece of equipment for the first time during a Tactical Scene usually does not take an Action. When a character uses a weapon, shield, tool or other equipment that was not yet in use, drawing it can be part of…
regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.text:
Drawing a piece of equipment for the first time during a Tactical Scene usually does not take an Action.
When a character uses a weapon, shield, tool or other equipment that was not yet in use, drawing it can be part of the Action itself.
For example, a character can draw their sword and start a Confront as part of the same Action.
Switch Equipment
Once the character already has equipment in use, replacing it with something else takes the Switch Equipment Action.
This Action represents stowing, rearranging or replacing what the character is using with other available equipment. This also covers dropping a piece of equipment on the ground to take another.
The switch can involve a single item or a set of equipment, as long as the change can reasonably be done during the Turn.
For example, a character could use Switch Equipment to:
swap a sword for a bow;
stow a weapon and equip a shield;
swap weapon and shield for a weapon that needs both hands;
replace the set of equipment currently in use with another prepared set.
The chosen equipment counts as in use as soon as the Action is done.
Drawing is not Switching
Using a piece of equipment for the first time does not count as a switch.
An Action is only needed when the character has to replace equipment that was already in use.
Taking a piece of equipment with a free hand is also drawing, even if the character already has other equipment in use. For example, a character with a sword in one hand can draw a dagger with the other without using Switch Equipment.
Picking up equipment from the ground is not drawing: it takes the Switch Equipment Action, even with a free hand. This includes recovering a weapon lost to Disarm.

regras/resistencia-e-vulnerabilidade/res.title: Resistance and Vulnerability
regras/resistencia-e-vulnerabilidade/res.summary: This section gathers the rules that define how characters and creatures react to damage from specific Damage Types and Materials, through Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities. They can be granted by equipment…
regras/resistencia-e-vulnerabilidade/res.text:
This section gathers the rules that define how characters and creatures react to damage from specific Damage Types and Materials, through Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities.
They can be granted by equipment, Conditions, origins, creatures, spells or effects.
Concepts
Resistance — a value that helps convert aggravated damage into superficial damage.
Vulnerability — a value that reduces absorption and increases the damage taken.
Immunity — no value; damage of the Type or Material simply does not apply.
Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities to Materials are, for now, set directly on characters and creatures. Armor still grants Resistances only to Damage Types.
Effective Absorption
When taking damage, the Effective Absorption is calculated considering the Damage Type taken and the Material of the weapon that caused it, if any:
Effective Absorption = total Absorption (base Absorption + armor Absorption) + Σ Resistances to the Type and the Material - Σ Vulnerabilities to the Type and the Material
The values for the Type and the Material are added together. When the damage source has no Material, only the Damage Type is considered.
Effective Absorption greater than or equal to the aggravated damage: all the damage is converted into superficial damage.
Effective Absorption between 0 and the damage: only the part covered by the absorption is converted; the rest stays aggravated (see Armor).
Negative Effective Absorption: the negative value is added to the damage taken (as an absolute value) and all the damage is aggravated — no conversion is possible (see Vulnerability).
Damage that is already superficial is not affected by positive absorption.
Immunity to the Type or the Material takes precedence over everything: the damage is ignored before Effective Absorption is even calculated, even if there is Vulnerability to the other.
Examples
A character with Absorption 1 and Fire Resistance 3 takes 4 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is 4, and the 4 points are converted into superficial damage.
A character with Fire Vulnerability 3 and Absorption 0 takes 1 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is -3, and they take 4 aggravated Fire damage.
A character with Fire Immunity takes 4 Fire damage: the damage does not apply, and no damage is taken.
A character with Absorption 2 and Fire Vulnerability 3 takes 1 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is -1, and they take 2 aggravated Fire damage.
A creature with Absorption 0, Slashing Resistance 3 and Silver Vulnerability 3 takes Slashing damage from a Silver weapon: the Effective Absorption is 0, since the values cancel out.
A creature with Common metal Immunity takes damage from an iron or steel weapon: no damage is taken, whatever the weapon's Damage Type. This Immunity does not apply to Silver or Meteorite weapons.
Relations
Damage Types and Materials are defined in Weapons. The severity of damage and its recovery are described in Health.
Damage dealt by Zones does not use Effective Absorption. In that case, each point of Resistance converts 1 point of the Zone's aggravated damage into superficial before applying the test's Successes, Vulnerabilities directly increase the Zone's Damage and Immunities prevent the damage entirely.

regras/condicoes/condicoes.summary: A Condition is a state that affects a character during a Scene, imposing mechanical effects while it stays active. Conditions are applied by Actions, Maneuvers, Capabilities or other rules. They are all gathered here as…
regras/condicoes/condicoes.text:
A Condition is a state that affects a character during a Scene, imposing mechanical effects while it stays active.
Conditions are applied by Actions, Maneuvers, Capabilities or other rules. They are all gathered here as the single core reference.
Conditions
Prone — on the ground; penalizes their own rolls and changes Attacks made against them.
Grappled — held by another character; no movement.
Debilitated — Health track full.
Slowed — reduced Movement until the next Turn of whoever applied it.
Shaken — penalty on the next Attack.
Poisoned — penalty on Physical rolls.
Paralyzed — no Action and no Movement.
Stunned — no Action.
Fear — stacking penalty on every Pool.
Aiming — stacks the bonus of the Aim Maneuver for the next ranged Attack.
Read — analyzed by another character; no effect of its own, used by Capabilities.
Challenged — provoked by a Duelist; penalizes Confronts started against other creatures.
Relations
Conditions are usually applied by Maneuvers and other effects during Scenes and Conflicts.

A Grappled character suffers the following effects.
Movement 0
When making an Attack against any target other than the character grappling them, the Grappled character gets:
-2 dice on the Dice Pool
Attacks made against whoever is holding the grapple do not suffer this penalty.
The character holding the grapple can drag or carry the target while moving, as long as the target is of the same Size or smaller. This movement is treated as Special Movement and follows the rules that apply to that kind of movement.
How to escape
During their Turn, a Grappled character can use their Action to try to escape.
To do so, they make a new opposed roll against the character holding the grapple:
Grappled character: Strength + Athletics
Character holding the grapple: Strength + Athletics
Capabilities and other rules can replace these Pools. The way the attempt is described does not allow freely swapping the Attribute or the Skill.
If the Grappled character gets more Successes, the Grappled Condition ends. On a tie or a win for the character holding the grapple, the condition remains.

Read is applied, for example, by the Mentalist's Cold Read and the Hunter's Know the Prey.

regras/condicoes/desafiado.text:
A Challenged character was provoked by a Duelist to remain in combat against them.
The Condition belongs to the Duelist who applied it. The Challenged character takes a dice penalty equal to that Duelist's Level when starting a Confront against any other creature.
Challenged ends at the end of the Scene or when the Duelist who applied the Condition starts a Confront against another creature.
